Paseo Dominical Muévete en Bici

Muévete en Bici car-free Sunday

Mexico City, Mexico · Paseo de la Reforma and the Centro Histórico · Open streets · Social

FamilyBeginner friendly

Paseo Dominical Muévete en Bici is an open-streets program in Mexico City, Mexico: streets closed to cars and open to bikes. It runs every Sunday from 8:00 am local time.

Next ride Sun, Oct 4, 8:00 AM CST

Amexi (Sept 20, 2026) says the Paseo Dominical Muévete en Bici runs 8:00 am to 2:00 pm on Reforma, Calzada de Guadalupe, División del Norte, Patriotismo, Eje 7 Sur, the Centro Histórico and Coyoacán; Amexi (Sept 13) gives the same hours (fetched Oct 1, 2026).

For visitors

Free, no sign-up. Join and leave anywhere on the route. Bike rental (including kids bikes and bikes for riders with disabilities), basic mechanics and medical help along the route. On ozone-alert days it can still run; watch the air-quality notice.

First time? Here's the drill

Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 8:00 am. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Pace isn't posted. Ask the host before you go, or say you're new when you arrive.
Check
Check the links below the day of for cancellations and weather calls.

About the Paseo Dominical Muévete en Bici group ride

Mexico City's car-free Sunday. Big avenues close to cars and fill with bikes, skaters and walkers until 2:00 pm. Ride a few kilometres or the whole loop; it is the easy way to see the city by bike on your first weekend.
